deep.reconstruction:
Context: in these 1953 notes Grothendieck builds an abstract theory of rearrangement-invariant convex functionals on L^∞ of an interval (]0,ω[ or ]0,∞[). The aim is to give a continuous, measure-theoretic form of the Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya and Weyl majorization inequalities. The likely application is to eigenvalue and singular-value inequalities for compact, nuclear or p-summing operators in his Fredholm-theory work of the same period.

Definitions from the previous page:
- A 'fonction de Pólya' P on L^∞(]0,ω[) satisfies P_1 (invariance under equimeasurable rearrangement), P_2 (convexity) and P_3 (weak or normal lower semicontinuity).
- Via Hahn–Banach applied to the epigraph, together with the Hardy–Littlewood rearrangement inequality, P is represented as P(f) = sup_i (a_i + ∫ φ_i φ_f). Here φ_f is the decreasing rearrangement of f and the φ_i are decreasing L^1 kernels.
- A 'fonction de Weyl' W on (L^∞)^+(]0,ω[) is one for which f ↦ W(exp f) is a Pólya function. This is the multiplicative (log-) analogue: Weyl's 1949 condition on products of eigenvalues versus singular values.
- On ]0,∞[, the definitions are imposed on all restrictions to ]0,ω[.

This page:
1. Examples. Let α: R^+ → [0,+∞] with α(0)=0 and s ↦ α(exp s) convex. Then W_α(f) = ∫_0^∞ α(f) is a Weyl function. It is increasing iff α is increasing. Indeed W_α(exp f) = ∫ (α∘exp)(f), which is the standard convex, rearrangement-invariant, lsc integral functional. For α_p(s) = s^p (0<p<∞) this gives W(f) = N_p(f)^p = ∫|f|^p. This is the functional behind Weyl's inequality Σ|λ_n|^p ≤ Σ s_n^p.
2. Extension. An increasing Weyl function on (L^∞)^+(]0,∞[) extends canonically to all positive measurable functions (the space written (K^∞)^+ or similar). On an arbitrary measure space M, set W(f) = sup{W(g) : 0 ≤ g ≤ f, g bounded}.
   - Then W(0) ≤ W(f) ≤ +∞.
   - W(f) depends only on the decreasing rearrangement: W(f) = W(φ_f).
   - The set {W < +∞} is directed, and W is increasing there.
   This is the usual Fatou-type (monotone lower) extension used for rearrangement-invariant function norms. The page stops mid-argument.
errors: The parenthetical gloss 'i.e. α(s^λ t^{1-λ}) ≤ α(s)^λ α(t)^{1-λ}' expresses log-convexity of s ↦ α(exp s). That is strictly stronger than the stated (and needed) convexity of α(exp s), which reads α(s^λ t^{1-λ}) ≤ λα(s) + (1-λ)α(t). The two coincide in strength only in special cases such as α = s^p, where both hold. The proof that W_α is a Weyl function needs only plain convexity.
Normalisations such as α(0)=0 (needed for ∫_0^∞ α(f) to make sense on ]0,∞[) and the possible value +∞ are stated only sketchily. Lower semicontinuity of α, needed for P_3, is not mentioned.
The canonical extension is stated, but on this page it is not shown to agree with W on bounded functions or to again be a Weyl function. That is presumably done later.

ideas.what: Abstract 'Weyl functions': functionals W on positive functions such that W∘exp is a convex, rearrangement-invariant, lsc functional. This is a continuous, measure-space version of Weyl's multiplicative majorization.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl (log-)majorization; functionals Φ with Φ∘exp convex (Weyl 1949, Ky Fan, Gohberg–Krein symmetric norming functions; continuous log-majorization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Weyl (1949); Pólya (1950); Ky Fan; Gohberg–Krein (1965); continuous majorization by Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (1929), Ryff, Luxemburg (1960s)
ideas.where_published: Weyl-type eigenvalue inequalities are used in Grothendieck's 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955). The abstract 'fonction de Weyl' framework itself appears unpublished.

ideas.what: Example W_α(f) = ∫α(f) with α∘exp convex, specialising to ∫|f|^p.
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's inequality Σ φ(|λ_n|) ≤ Σ φ(s_n) for φ with φ(e^t) convex increasing

ideas.what: Canonical extension of an increasing rearrangement-invariant functional from bounded positive functions to all positive measurable functions on any measure space, via sup over 0 ≤ g ≤ f. The extension depends only on the decreasing rearrangement.
ideas.modern_name: Fatou-property extension of rearrangement-invariant function norms / Lorentz–Luxemburg r.i. spaces

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck sets up a general continuous (measure-space) theory of multiplicative (Weyl) majorization. Weyl functions are defined by requiring W∘exp to be a rearrangement-invariant convex lsc functional, with a duality representation and canonical extension. This parallels later work on continuous majorization and r.i. spaces (Ryff, Luxemburg, Calderón) and on symmetric norming functions (Gohberg–Krein), and it is not part of his published record. The individual results are classical or near-routine, so the interest is mainly historical.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence of how Grothendieck approached eigenvalue distributions of nuclear/p-summing operators through an abstract log-majorization framework. It is of modest mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an unpublished, systematic abstraction of Weyl's log-majorization to rearrangement-invariant functionals on measure spaces, a decade before comparable systematic treatments. The actual statements (W_α examples, Fatou-type extension) are standard, and continuous HLP majorization was already known in 1929.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'nulle à l'origine [?] et =+∞ [?]' is likely 'nulle à l'origine, et ≤ +∞' (i.e. α may take the value +∞); the reading is uncertain.
'(K^∞)^+(]0,+∞[)' probably denotes the space of all measurable (possibly unbounded) positive functions, e.g. (L^0)^+ or M^+, rather than a space 'K^∞'.
'W(f) = W(f_1), et si f_1 est une réarrangée décroissante (W(f) = W(φ_{f_1}))' is better read as: W(f) depends only on f through its decreasing rearrangement, W(f) = W(φ_f).
The marginal insertion reads '(sup étendu à l'ensemble des ...)' and qualifies 'W(f) = sup W(g)'.
